definitions.explanation: A forest that has grown naturally rather than being planted by humans. Contrasted with {人工林|じんこうりん} (plantation forest). Used in forestry, ecology, and environmental discussions.

examples.japanese: {自然林|しぜんりん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{自然林|しぜんりん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{覆|おお}われている→覆う：02020_oou⟧。
examples.english: This mountain is covered by natural forest that has existed for ages.

examples.japanese: {自然林|しぜんりん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{人工林|じんこうりん}⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多様|たよう}→多様：12180_tayou⟧な⟦{生物|せいぶつ}→生物：03295_seibutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。

examples.english: It takes decades to restore a logged natural forest to its original state.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧ (nature, natural) and {林|りん} (forest, woods). A forest in which the trees have grown from natural seed dispersal rather than being deliberately planted. It typically contains a mix of species and age classes, in contrast to the uniform rows of a plantation forest.

USAGE:
Common in forestry policy, environmental reporting, and nature writing. Sometimes used loosely to mean any forest that feels "wild," even if it has experienced minor human activity.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自然林|しぜんりん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧: to protect natural forests
- {自然林|しぜんりん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{再生|さいせい}→再生：04442_saisei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to restore natural forests
- {自然林|しぜんりん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧: natural forest remains
- ⟦{豊|ゆた}か→豊か：03654_yutaka⟧な{自然林|しぜんりん}: a rich natural forest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天然林|てんねんりん}: natural forest — a near-synonym, more common in forestry terminology
- ⟦{原始林|げんしりん}→原始林：23672_genshirin⟧: primeval forest — a stricter term for completely undisturbed forest
- {人工林|じんこうりん}: plantation forest — the direct antonym; planted and managed by humans
- ⟦{雑木林|ぞうきばやし}→雑木林：27915_zoukibayashi⟧: mixed woodland, coppice — a small natural forest of mixed broadleaf trees, often near villages
